name: Self-Ask (+ Search) — Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023 (ACL Anthology 2023.findings-emnlp.378, pages 5687-5711); originally arXiv Oct 2022
authors_affiliation: Ofir Press, Muru Zhang, Sewon Min, Ludwig Schmidt, Noah A. Smith, Mike Lewis. Primary affiliation: Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, University of Washington; with MosaicML, Meta AI Research, and Allen Institute for AI (AI2).
task_domain: QA — compositional multi-hop open-domain question answering (factual reasoning).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, few-shot prompting of a frozen large language model (GPT-3 family, e.g. InstructGPT text/code Davinci-002 and vanilla Davinci) with no fine-tuning. The work first measures the 'compositionality gap' (the fraction of multi-hop questions answered wrong even though the model answers all sub-questions correctly) and then narrows it. Self-Ask prompts the LM to explicitly emit and answer follow-up sub-questions before the final answer; Self-Ask + Search Engine (SA+SE) routes each emitted follow-up sub-question to an external internet search engine API instead of the LM, inserting the returned answer back into the prompt. No supervised training; only few-shot in-context demonstrations.
what_is_retrieved: Search-engine answers (featured snippets / first-result extracted text) for the LM-generated follow-up sub-questions. In SA+SE the retrieved item is the search engine's answer to a natural-language sub-question.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus — a live internet search engine API over the web (no agent-written growing memory). Retrieval grounds against an external, web-scale, continuously-updatable source.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Effectively top-1: for each follow-up sub-question the search engine returns a single answer (featured snippet, else the first search result's extracted text); the objective is to answer each decomposed sub-question correctly rather than to retrieve a fixed top-k document ranking.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A — not a case-based reasoning method (no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False — the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: snippet — a search-engine answer string (featured snippet or first-result extracted text) per LM-generated follow-up sub-question.
index_source: Static external web index served by a popular internet search engine API; no offline-induced or test-time-induced store is built by the method.
index_structure_topology: flat — an external search-engine web index queried by natural-language sub-questions; no method-side graph/hierarchical/cluster structure.
retriever_type: External internet search engine API (commercial web search, e.g. Google via SerpAPI in the released demo); not BM25/dense/learned in the method itself — the retriever is an off-the-shelf web search service. LM-as-query-generator + search-engine-as-retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf) — the search engine is used as-is with no training; query generation is produced by the frozen LM via few-shot prompting, not by a trained retriever.
query_construction: Decomposed sub-queries: the LM emits explicit follow-up sub-questions (after the trigger phrase 'Follow up:'); each full sub-question is sent verbatim as the query to the search engine.
query_granularity: step-level — one query per follow-up sub-question step within the decomposition (iterative, multiple sub-queries per main question), not a single task-level query.
when_to_retrieve: iterative — retrieval is triggered each time the LM emits a follow-up sub-question, repeating until the LM outputs the final answer; agent-initiated (the LM decides how many follow-ups to ask).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: the LM's emission of a 'Follow up:' sub-question (terminated by the 'Intermediate answer:' cue) triggers a search-engine call. The number and timing of retrievals are decided by the LM's own generated decomposition (not a fixed schedule or token-confidence signal).
reranking: None — no reranking stage; the search engine's featured snippet (or first result) is taken directly.
retrieved_context_refinement: Largely none for SA+SE (the returned answer is inserted back into the prompt). A separate baseline 'Search Engine + LM postprocessing' uses Davinci-002 to extract the short final answer from full-sentence search results, but in SA+SE itself no explicit refinement/compression/distractor-filtering is applied.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — no tool/skill descriptions are indexed; the search engine is a single fixed tool invoked with the natural-language sub-question.
index_content_separation: N/A — no separate lightweight index vs heavy content; queries go straight to a web search engine.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Live external search-engine web index (continuously updatable), accessed via a search-engine API (e.g. SerpAPI/Google in the released code). No MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling formalism; integration is a few lines of code feeding sub-questions to the API and inserting results back into the prompt.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A — a single search tool; no inter-tool dependency modeling.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the search engine's answer to each follow-up sub-question is inserted back into the prompt (as if the LM had produced 'Intermediate answer: ...'), and the LM continues generating the next sub-question or the final answer. Retrieved evidence is consumed in-context, not used as a training signal or latent injection.
planning_integration: Inside a decompose-then-search loop: the LM plans by decomposing the question into follow-up sub-questions; retrieval is interleaved per sub-question within the reasoning chain (retrieve-then-continue), repeating until a final answer. This is per-step interleaved retrieval inside a self-generated decomposition, not one-shot plan-time exemplars or tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-sub-question (per decomposition step): one search-engine call per LM-emitted follow-up question within a single rollout.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A — not CBR; no retrieved case is adapted. (The closest analogue is that the search answer is spliced verbatim into the in-context decomposition.)
retrieved_item_representation: Raw text answer (featured snippet or extracted first-result text) inserted as 'Intermediate answer:' into the free-text decomposition transcript; surface form is a short natural-language answer string.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw factual answer to a single sub-question (atomic fact / snippet), not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Minimal/none explicit. The structured Self-Ask scaffolding (clear sub-question demarcation) plus the optional LM-postprocessing baseline to extract short answers mitigate format/noise issues, but there is no retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, or reason-in-documents refinement in SA+SE.
memory_type: none — the method uses no episodic/skill/workflow memory; it relies on a stateless external search engine plus the in-context prompt transcript.
write_back: False — no experiences/cases/skills are written back to any memory store.
online_growth: False — no method-side store grows during deployment (the underlying web index updates externally, but the method itself maintains no growing memory).
write_back_trigger: never — nothing is written back to a memory.
failure_experience_usage: N/A — no storage or reuse of failed/negative experiences (no memory).
memory_evolution_update: N/A — no stored entries to mutate (no memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False — retrieval is not a learned/RL policy; sub-question emission is produced by a frozen few-shot-prompted LM and queries go to an off-the-shelf search engine.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A — single-agent, single-LM; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: Compositional Celebrities (CC, ~8.6k automatically generated 2-hop questions, 17 templates, introduced by this paper); Bamboogle (125 hand-written 2-hop questions, introduced by this paper, filtered so a search engine's featured snippet is wrong); 2WikiMultiHopQA (Ho et al., 2020); MuSiQue / Musique (Trivedi et al., 2022).
baselines: Direct Prompting (few-shot, Brown et al. 2020); Chain of Thought (Wei et al. 2022b); plain Search Engine (question sent directly to search engine); Search Engine + LM postprocessing (Davinci-002 extracts the short answer from search results); 'Let's think step by step' zero-shot CoT (Kojima et al. 2022) is discussed but not extensively run. Self-Ask is also compared against these; Self-Ask + Search is the proposed extension.
key_metrics: Accuracy (%). For Bamboogle, accuracy is manually judged by the authors; for 2WikiMultiHopQA and MuSiQue, exact match (EM). Also reports speed as average number of tokens in the generated answer.
headline_result: On Bamboogle with Davinci-002, Self-Ask + Search Engine reaches 60.0% accuracy vs 57.6% Self-Ask, 46.4% Chain of Thought, 17.6% Direct Prompting, and 0.0% for plain search. Self-Ask + Search also leads on 2WikiMultiHopQA (40.1% EM) and MuSiQue (15.2% EM). Separately, the paper's central measurement is that the compositionality gap stays roughly constant at ~40% across GPT-3 model sizes (1B–175B), not shrinking with scale.
ablations: Table 1 (Davinci-002): Direct prompting 17.6/25.4/5.6, Chain of Thought 46.4/29.8/12.6, plain Search 0.0/2.2/1.5, Search+postproc. -/26.3/6.5, Self-ask 57.6/30.0/13.8, Self-ask+Search 60.0/40.1/15.2 on Bamboogle/2Wiki/MuSiQue respectively — isolating the marginal gains of (a) elicitive decomposition (Self-ask over CoT/Direct) and (b) plugging in the search engine (SA+SE over Self-ask). On CC, Self-Ask obtains 79.6%/54.2% with InstructGPT-Davinci-002/Davinci vs 45.7%/1.1% for 'Let's think step by step', showing decomposition prompting strongly beats zero-shot CoT. Format ablation: 40% of CoT final answers were not short-form vs 17% for Self-ask and 3% for Self-ask+search, showing the scaffolding improves answer parseability. Trigger-phrase ablation: appending 'Are follow up questions needed here:' slightly improves results (more so for smaller models).
evaluation_decoupling: Partly. The compositionality gap is an intrinsic decomposition metric (sub-question correctness vs full-question correctness) reported on CC, separate from end-to-end accuracy; but no Recall@k/nDCG retrieval metrics are reported (the retriever is an external search engine).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Final-answer accuracy/EM is the outcome metric; the compositionality gap measures intermediate sub-question vs final reasoning quality (a process-level metric), and the short-form-answer-rate analysis assesses process/format quality.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reports speed as average number of generated answer tokens (Table 2) and notes the search-engine integration is implementable in only a few lines of code and requires no fine-tuning or architecture change. SA+SE makes one search-engine API call per follow-up sub-question (typically a few per 2-hop question). No detailed dollar/latency cost study beyond token-count speed.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Few-shot prompting with task-specific demonstrations (e.g. a 4-shot prompt for Bamboogle); the SA+SE prompt is identical to the Self-Ask prompt. Retrieval selection count is top-1 per sub-question (featured snippet, else first result). No fixed token budget cap reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A — this is a method/measurement paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Compositional Celebrities: ~8.6k automatically generated 2-hop questions composed from frequently stated facts combined in improbable ways, covering 17 templates; designed to estimate the compositionality gap at scale, answers programmatically verifiable. Bamboogle: 125 hand-crafted 2-hop questions written by the authors, each verifiable from Wikipedia but filtered so a popular search engine returns an incorrect featured snippet; designed for diverse, high-variation evaluation with less statistical power. (2WikiMultiHopQA and MuSiQue are pre-existing automatically generated multi-hop datasets.)
builds_on: Few-shot in-context prompting (GPT-3, Brown et al. 2020); Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022b); scratchpad/elicitive prompting (Nye et al. 2021); zero-shot CoT 'Let's think step by step' (Kojima et al. 2022). Uses GPT-3 family models (InstructGPT/Davinci) off-the-shelf and a commercial internet search engine API.
contrasts_with: Direct (naive) few-shot prompting; Chain-of-Thought prompting (Self-Ask disentangles question decomposition from sub-answer generation and yields more parseable answers); plain search-engine QA (which fails on these composed questions, 0.0% on Bamboogle); 'Let's think step by step' zero-shot CoT (much weaker on CC).
lineage: Sub-topic B (RAG for task solving): an early (2022/2023) decompose-then-search / interleaved reasoning-and-retrieval method for compositional multi-hop QA, alongside contemporaneous work like ReAct and IRCoT; a foundational predecessor for agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning where an LM emits sub-questions answered by an external search tool.
